newsitem.title: USA: Transvestite pleads guilty to killing two policemen.
newsitem.headline: Transvestite pleads guilty to killing two policemen.

text.p: A transsexual pleaded guilty on Tuesday to two counts of felony murder stemming from a 1995 shootout with three police officers which was followed by a 12-hour standoff that only ended when police met her demand for makeup.

Leslie Nelson pleaded guilty in Superior Court to killing two police officers in the line of duty. A Mercer County jury will decide next week whether Nelsen should face the death penalty or serve a minimum of 30 years in jail without parole.

Haddon Heights police officer John Norcross and Camden County investigator John McLaughlin were killed in a hail of automatic gunfire in April 1995 when they went to confiscate guns from Nelson's house. The shooting lasted only a matter of seconds.
Norcross' brother, Richard, survived with four gunshot wounds.

The two officers were investigating complaints that the 6-foot-2-inch Nelson had been bothering neighbourhood children. After they spotted the weapons, they obtained a search warrant and McLaughlin's help in executing it.
Nelson was arrested after a 12-hour standoff. She surrendered when police met her demand for the makeup.
